# Drinks

*Page PDF 16*

## **Drinks**
The most obvious attraction taverns offer to their clients is a place to consume alcoholic drinks. This does not mean a landlord will tolerate patrons becoming conspicuously drunk, some of them are even conscientious enough to keep an eye out for signs of problem drinking. However, as the consumption of ale lines their pockets, most of them are happy to serve any customer capable of standing up. 

## **Ale (a)**
Ubiquitous and popular, a venue without a stock of ale can hardly be considered a tavern. Beer, mead, or cider may be served instead of, or alongside, ale for a similar price. 

_**Examples:** Eilhart Brown, Forlorn Hops, Kiegel’s Natural Pig Swill, Marienburg Pale, Old Dog Puke, Shramleben Dark Ale_ **Fair Price:** 3d for a pint. **Average (+20) Consume Alcohol** Test per pint. 

**Rough Spirits (RS)** 

Cheap brandies, schnapps, and liqueurs with a pronounced bitter taste. 

## **Dwarf Ale (Da)**
The most celebrated ales by renowned Dwarf breweries. 

_**Examples of other Dwarf ales:** Bugman’s Castle XXXXXXXXX, Bugman’s Special Brew, Durgrund’s Hellfire, Korben’s Finest, Old Fortitude, One-finger’s Tar Drop, Thengeln’s Golden Preserve, Troll Brew, Zhufbar Ale_ **Fair Price:** 9d for a pint. Three **Average (+20) Consume Alcohol** Tests per pint. 

## **Excellent Spirits (Es)**
Brandies, schnapps, and liqueurs of fine quality. 

_**Examples:** Albion Uisce, Alte Geheerentode Rum, Echte Brandenburger (the Emperor’s favourite brandy)_ **Fair Price:** 8d per shot, 4/- for a pint bottle (8 shots). **Average (+20) Consume Alcohol** Test per shot. 

_**Examples:** Dwarf Gragrint, Kislevite Samogon, Orc Bitters_ **Fair Price:** 2d per shot, 1/- for a pint bottle (8 shots). **Average (+20) Consume Alcohol** Test per shot. 

## **Spirits (S)**
Brandies, schnapps, and liqueurs of average quality. 

_**Examples:** Egling Geist, Eilhart Obstler, Oberwil Infusion_ **Fair Price:** 4d per shot, 2/- for a pint bottle (8 shots). **Average (+20) Consume Alcohol** Test per shot. 

## **Small Beer (SB)**
Watered-down ale is often sold openly in cheap taverns. It may be weak and tasteless, but it is still safer than drinking water. 

**Fair Price:** 2d for a pint. **Easy (+40) Consume Alcohol** Test per pint. 

## **Fine Wine (Fw)**
Respectable vintages from reliable sources. 

_**Examples:** Gewürzstraminek Dessert Wine, Grenzstadter Deep Wine, Pritzstock Riesling, Whistler’s Finest Rose Wine_ **Fair Price:** 8d per glass, 2/8 per bottle (5 glasses). **Average (+20) Consume Alcohol** Test per glass. 

## **Legendary Wine (Lw)**
The best wines come from Bretonnia and Tilea, and which nation produces the superior wine is cause for ineluctable debate between connoisseurs. Few wines in the Empire can compare, though a batch from a famous year may achieve renown. 

_**Examples:** Annaliese, Bilbali Vino Tinto, Gewürzstraminek 08, Manann’s Own, Morceaux Vin Sec, Ravolan Frizzante_ **Fair Price:** Prices can reach extortionate costs and start at no less than 4/- per glass, 18/- per bottle (5 glasses). **Average (+20) Consume Alcohol** Test per glass. 

## **Strong Ale (Sa)**
The result of more exacting and time-consuming brewing processes, strong ales are more expensive than regular ales but admired for their flavour and alcoholic kick. 

_**Examples:** Braakbroew Ale, Orc’s Headwrecker, Stromdorf Gewitterwasser_ 

**Fair Price:** 5d for a pint. **Challenging (+0) Consume Alcohol** Test per pint. 

## **Wine (W)**
The Empire’s climate may not be the best for viticulture, but their Hocks and Rieslings still have their admirers. 

_**Examples:** Aulenbacher, Gewürzstraminek Hock, Heisenberg Rotwein, Loningbruck Ruby, Wurtbader Weißwein_ **Fair Price:** 4d per glass, 1/4 per bottle (5 glasses). **Average (+20) Consume Alcohol** Test per glass.
